title: Ship the 4-Gate Salesforce Sync: Retire the Daily CSV Export in 20 Minutes
subtitle: For RevOps and ops leads at $1M-$20M service firms running one person's morning export as critical infrastructure. Get a scheduled, validated n8n job instead.

sections.title: Map what the export actually does
sections.description: Before you automate the morning CSV, write down what it pulls and where it lands, so the workflow matches reality and not the version in someone's head.

items.text: Pull up the exact Salesforce report your team exports each morning and copy its filters
items.tip: Write down the object, fields, and date range. This becomes your SOQL query, so 'which report did Dana use' never comes up again.

items.text: Trace where the CSV lands today and which reports read from it downstream
items.tip: Sheet, warehouse, or CRM. The list of downstream readers tells you which fields are non-negotiable.

items.text: List every field your downstream reports break without
items.tip: Id, Name, StageName at minimum. This list goes straight into the REQUIRED schema gate.

items.text: Record a normal day's row count from the last week of exports
items.tip: You'll set the row-count floor to roughly 50% of this number so a broken pull halts instead of publishing 12 rows.

sections.title: Import the workflow and wire credentials
sections.description: The JSON lands inactive, so you can connect everything before a single run fires.

items.text: Import the workflow JSON via the top-right menu in n8n
items.tip: Use Import from File or paste into Import from Clipboard. It arrives inactive and prompts you to map credentials.

items.text: Connect the three credentials on the red-flagged nodes: Salesforce OAuth2, Google Sheets, Slack
items.tip: Click each flagged node and pick the credential. n8n maps it everywhere the cred is used automatically.

items.text: Open Query Salesforce and swap the SOQL for your object and field list
items.tip: Default pulls Opportunity modified since yesterday. Match it to the report you copied in section one.

items.text: Drop your Sheet ID and tab name into the Write to Destination node
items.tip: Google Sheets is the demo target because you can verify it in 30 seconds. Swap it later for your real target.

sections.title: Set the 4 validation gates
sections.description: This is the part that makes the job safe to run unattended. Without it, you've just automated publishing bad data faster.

items.text: Set MIN_ROWS to about half a normal day's pull in the 4-Gate Validation node
items.tip: If you usually get 200 rows and one morning you get 12, that should halt, not publish.

items.text: Add every downstream-critical field to the REQUIRED array
items.tip: This is your early warning for a renamed or deleted Salesforce field. A blank column trips here before a chart breaks.

items.text: Match the freshness window to your run cadence
items.tip: 24h assumes a daily job. Widen it for a weekly run, or the gate flags a stale pull that isn't actually stale.

items.text: Confirm the dedupe key is genuinely unique for your object
items.tip: Id is the safe default. A re-run or bad join shows up here instead of double-counting pipeline at quarter-end.

sections.title: Test the failure path, then go live
sections.description: An automation you check manually anyway defeats the point. Prove the safety net catches a bad pull before you trust it at 6am.

items.text: Trigger the workflow manually once and confirm a clean pass writes to the destination
items.tip: Watch the execution. Validated rows go down the pass branch; nothing should hit the Slack alert.

items.text: Set MIN_ROWS to 99999, run it, and confirm you get the Slack alert with the destination untouched
items.tip: If the sheet stays empty and the alert names the exact reason, your safety net works. Set MIN_ROWS back after.

items.text: Verify the Salesforce node is set to retry 3 times with a 5-second wait
items.tip: A transient API blip at 6am retries instead of firing a false alarm. It ships configured this way already.

items.text: Toggle the workflow active and let the weekday 6am schedule take over
items.tip: The job no longer depends on a person remembering. Sick days stop costing you a missing day of data.

sections.title: Swap in your real destination
sections.description: Once the demo run passes, replace the single pass-branch node with whatever your data actually feeds.

items.text: Delete the Google Sheets node and wire in your real target on the pass branch
items.tip: Postgres or BigQuery for a warehouse, Airtable for a base, HTTP Request for any REST endpoint. The gates and alert stay untouched.

items.text: Use Upsert on Id if your target is a database so re-runs stay safe
items.tip: Postgres or warehouse upsert on the Salesforce Id means a second run updates rows instead of duplicating them.
